headline: Executive order places new import taxes (duties) on goods from China, tied to concerns about the supply of synthetic opioids like fentanyl.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order imposes duties, which are taxes on imported goods, on products connected to China. The stated reason is to address the supply chain for synthetic opioids that comes from China. The title does not give the duty rates, which goods are covered, or any exceptions.

who_it_affects.group: US businesses that import goods from China
who_it_affects.how: They would owe the new duties when bringing covered Chinese products into the country.

who_it_affects.group: Companies in China that sell goods to the US
who_it_affects.how: Their products would face added taxes when entering the US market.

who_it_affects.group: US shoppers who buy products made in China
who_it_affects.how: Duties paid by importers can lead to higher prices on affected goods, though the title does not say which goods are covered.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed February 1, 2025; the exact start date for the duties is not stated in the provided source.
